event.summary: Proxy sampling wording does not establish stale creation settings
event.detail: Reviewed commit: c8bc155cc36723c8c53870944d07ce8ec61ef9ed. TLDR: Investigated whether new containers must inherit stale proxy settings sampled by an earlier background host probe. No stale-settings route is established by this documentation-only commit. SPEC_impl.md 6561–6564 says to read proxy variables during the place probe, but does not say that only a previously cached background probe may supply creation settings or forbid a creation-time probe. SPEC.md 4802–4804 explicitly requires creation-time inheritance: "Containers inherit proxy variables from the container host's systemd user manager environment at creation." It also says, "Later host changes affect newly created containers." The full SPEC_impl.md introduction (lines 3–6) resolves observable disagreements: "SPEC.md defines what the product does; when this document and SPEC.md disagree about observable behavior, SPEC.md wins." Checks: delivered all assigned contract patch text, read complete Disposable environments and Container sessions sections, searched all proxy/show-environment references in both pinned specifications, and inspected commit stat (only SPEC.md and SPEC_impl.md change). These checks show an implementation must refresh sufficiently to honor SPEC.md; this patch does not introduce code choosing old cache data. Suggested bucket: other for wording ambiguity only; could-be-highest: false, no established security or work-loss route, and no changed runtime path. Confidence: confirmed scope/contract analysis, not execution. proposed_drop: no concrete faulty implementation or contradictory mandatory choice; the product contract explicitly settles the required behavior. possible_cover: none. Preserved suspected consequence: an implementation using only an old cached probe could give new containers obsolete or absent proxy settings and prevent their network access; that would need source evidence in the implementation group. No runtime tests or reproductions run.

event.summary: New containers can permanently inherit a cached host proxy environment
event.detail: Reviewed commit: c8bc155cc36723c8c53870944d07ce8ec61ef9ed (assigned specification patch); verified implementation revision: 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db. TLDR: After the container host proxy settings change, a new container can keep the old settings for its entire lifetime, leaving its agents unable to reach the network even though it was launched after the change. The earlier design-only candidate is superseded by this established implementation route; the original consequence of stale or absent network proxy settings is preserved. Source route at tip: environment/podman.rs ensure_prepared 975–990 calls places.fresh, but podman_probe.rs 18–20 and 326–334 admit a cached observation up to 300 seconds old; fresh 385–406 immediately returns that observation. With an already prepared image, creation needs no intervening build. podman.rs 1183–1205 calls self.place and installs ready.proxy for the unadmitted container. self.place 148–164 calls places.runtime; podman_probe.rs 340–380 returns an existing success for the same route without any age check or forced read. Thus change the host manager proxy after an already completed probe while the launcher stays open, then launch within that five-minute freshness window: both admission and proxy installation consume the old observation. No further refresh is required by this path. podman.rs 1223–1227 deliberately preserves the installed snapshot after admission, so a later probe or reboot does not repair this new container. Contract at tip SPEC.md 4877–4879: "Containers inherit proxy variables from the container host's systemd user manager environment at creation." and "Later host changes affect newly created containers." Original contract is identical at SPEC.md 4802–4804. SPEC_impl.md 6561–6564 at the assigned revision says sampling occurs during a probe, but does not authorize old values for new containers; the SPEC_impl.md introduction explicitly gives SPEC.md precedence on observable behavior. Suggested bucket: other (established configuration-propagation correctness; no established security or user-work loss route). Could-be-highest: false on current evidence; no claim is made that stale proxies disclose credentials or bypass network policy. Confidence: confirmed by source/contract and callers, not execution. proposed_drop: false; no parent drop accepted. possible_cover: none (no forbidden coverage sources searched). Fix direction: separate fresh creation-time manager proxy sampling from reusable capability observations; preserve the deliberate no-rewrite behavior for environments already admitted. Caveats: the effect requires a manager-environment change after the observation and before the new container snapshot; refreshing after the change and waiting for it prevents this route. The 300-second bound applies before preparation, not necessarily to a lengthy preparation's final install, whose runtime cache has no age bound. No runtime tests or reproductions run.

event.summary: New containers can permanently inherit a cached host proxy environment
event.detail: Reviewed assigned contract commit: c8bc155cc36723c8c53870944d07ce8ec61ef9ed. Verified implementation revision: 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db; git blame attributes the creation-time self.place/proxies call to full commit 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b, which is in the supplied commit list. TLDR: After the container host proxy settings change, a newly launched container can keep the old or absent proxy settings for its lifetime, preventing its agents from reaching the network. This supersedes the original design-only candidate; its original suspected network consequence is preserved and now source-confirmed. At pinned tip provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs 377–398 admits cached place metadata and registers a fresh environment; environment_session_steps 521–555 performs ensure_prepared then create. environment/podman.rs 975–990 calls places.fresh before preparation. However podman_probe.rs 18–20 and 326–334 accept observations up to 300 seconds old, and fresh 385–406 returns such a cached result without refreshing. With an existing prepared image no intervening build is needed. Creation at podman.rs 1183–1205 gets ready.proxy through self.place at 1195. self.place 148–164 uses places.runtime; podman_probe.rs 340–380 accepts a same-route cached success without any age check or forced read. Thus after a completed launcher probe, change the host manager proxy while keeping that launcher open, then launch within five minutes: admission and installation both use the old snapshot. Probe source at podman_probe.rs 596–628 reads the manager only when probe runs, selects the proxy values, and returns them in ReadyPlace at 658–663. Installation is not a second read of the host manager: podman.rs proxies 558–638 reads the container manager only for XDG_CONFIG_HOME, renders the passed cached values at 588–589, installs their environment.d file at 612–614, and unsets/imports precisely those values at 621–636. The creation path then restarts the supervisor at 1214–1216. After admission, 1223–1227 deliberately refuses to rewrite the snapshot on later probes/retries/reboots, so this new container does not heal when the cache refreshes. Contract: original SPEC.md 4802–4804, unchanged at tip 4877–4879, says "Containers inherit proxy variables from the container host's systemd user manager environment at creation" and "Later host changes affect newly created containers." Original SPEC_impl.md 6561–6564 says read during a probe but never authorizes stale values for a later creation; its introduction gives SPEC.md precedence. Suggested bucket: other (configuration-propagation correctness); could-be-highest: false on established evidence. Confidence: confirmed by source/contract and caller trace; no execution observed. proposed_drop: false; no parent drop accepted. possible_cover: none; no forbidden coverage searches. Fix direction: sample the host manager proxy for the new environment at creation, independently of capability-cache reuse, while preserving existing admitted environments. Caveats: requires a host manager-environment change between observation and launch; an explicit completed refresh after that change avoids the route. Initial observation is bounded to five minutes before preparation, but a long preparation can age it further because installation uses the age-unbounded runtime cache. No security disclosure or loss-of-work route is claimed. No tests or reproductions run.

event.summary: Proposed drop: lost initial-create reply permits destroying the new environment
event.detail: Reviewed commit: c8bc155cc36723c8c53870944d07ce8ec61ef9ed. TLDR: If the first session starts but its creation reply is lost, failed-launch cleanup is allowed to destroy its newly created container, including the agent and any work it already wrote. This is a potentially highest loss-of-work consequence, explicitly accepted by the product contract; recorded as a finding with proposed_drop for the required independent acceptance check. Source: SPEC_impl.md, Environment ownership and refusal (6572–6592), says, "A failed normal initial launch may destroy only its new environment." SPEC.md, Container sessions (4762–4768), says, "An ordinary failed initial launch may discard its newly created container, including after a lost session-create reply." The governing Sandbox sessions section is explicit at 1464–1472: "If an ordinary new launch fails before the helm has confirmed session creation, including a lost create reply, it attempts to delete that newly created sandbox and snapshots" and "This may end an agent that started before its reply was lost." The same sections distinguish Replace: failed or ambiguous Replace preserves the existing environment and files. Suggested bucket: highest if this were unaccepted behavior (new agent work can be destroyed); could-be-highest: true. Confidence: confirmed accepted contract consequence, not an observed runtime bug; this commit edits specifications only, so no newly shipped destruction route is established by its diff. proposed_drop: exact product-spec acceptance quoted above; independent check required. possible_cover: none. Caveats: only an ordinary initial launch's own new environment may be cleaned this way; this acceptance does not excuse destruction during Replace or of unrelated resources. No runtime tests or reproductions run.

TLDR: An agent whose first creation reply to the helm is lost can already have written work when failed-initial-launch cleanup destroys its own newly allocated environment. Preserve this potentially highest loss-of-work consequence and proposed drop for independent checking; no parent drop accepted. Exact original acceptance: SPEC.md 4764–4766 says, "Failed or ambiguous Replace preserves the container and files" and "An ordinary failed initial launch may discard its newly created container, including after a lost session-create reply." SPEC_impl.md 6576–6578 says Replace preserves existing files and "A failed normal initial launch may destroy only its new environment." SPEC.md 1465–1470 explicitly says failed ordinary new launch, including lost create reply, attempts deletion and "This may end an agent that started before its reply was lost." At pinned tip the same initial-launch/Replace distinction remains in SPEC.md 4831–4837. Source checks now establish the route rather than relying only on design: provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs 388–398 allocates a fresh reserved name and registers a new session-owned row, retains that returned host through environment_session_steps and finish_session_launch at 479–485, and passes that exact captured host to first-session creation at 1019–1025. sessions.rs 1761–1803 uses that captured session-owned host; its ordinary create path propagates a client create error at 2077–2094. finish_session_launch 1040–1050 invokes whole-resource cleanup on that same host for an error, expressly including a lost create reply; successful creation at 1030–1038 takes no such cleanup. Browser/result-receiver loss is different: the owned task completes, and its final result.send at 1069 is ignored if the receiver is gone; losing the outer browser reply alone does not destroy a successfully confirmed session. hosts.rs 1506–1553 resolves the captured row's binding, invokes that provider's destroy, and requires returned proof before forgetting it. Podman destroy 1292–1333 resolves only its recorded canonical ID or pending-create reserved name, checks ownership for recovered IDs, and retains unsettled absence. remove_container at 400–414 rechecks this helm/session labels, removes the inspected canonical ID, and confirms absence. No source route to unrelated resources was established by these checks. Replace has a separate path: sessions.rs finish_replacement 4547–4647 sends client.delete_session_with for only the accepted replacement's source at 4575; failures report definite/ambiguous source outcomes rather than invoking whole-resource cleanup. Suggested bucket: highest for the preserved agent-work loss consequence if unaccepted; could-be-highest: true. Confidence: source-confirmed implementation and explicit specification acceptance, not execution. proposed_drop: exact initial-new-resource acceptance quoted above, pending independent caller decision. possible_cover: none. The acceptance does not cover Replace's existing resource, any unrelated environment, or normal successful create followed only by browser disconnection. It does not authorize cleanup after confirmed creation. No runtime tests or reproductions run.

event.detail: Reviewed contract commit: c8bc155cc36723c8c53870944d07ce8ec61ef9ed; source checks at inclusive tip 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db. TLDR: Considered whether sharing the recipe catalog and host storage could let an ordinary recipe save overwrite resource ownership, or let host removal/retargeting discard the route needed to clean up existing environments. Narrow source checks refute those paths; no reported defect or new runtime issue. Original contract at SPEC_impl.md 6436–6449 requires the complete kind/name/provider discriminator, reference-based place mutation refusal and cleanup proof before forgetting. Shared recipes at 6491ff/6782–6792 keeps independent definition and build-state writers. At tip store.rs HostKind::from_columns 798–815 matches all three columns and refuses unknown/inconsistent provider spellings. tensorlake/recipes.rs update_tensorlake_recipe 294–342 validates and writes only spec_json/updated_at in an immediate transaction; tensorlake/build.rs write_recipe_state 318–367 reads the current spec/state under an immediate transaction and writes only state_json. Thus these writers cannot clobber each other's column even if their requests race. delete_tensorlake_recipe 393–427 rechecks host use and needs_cleanup in the final immediate transaction before deletion. store/podman.rs refuse_referenced_place 213–250 checks every referring place_host row without filtering stopped/cleanup states and recipe per-place needs_cleanup; store.rs update_ssh_destination 7533–7567 invokes it inside its mutation transaction, and remove_host_row 8034–8065 invokes it inside the removal transaction and requires the row-specific destruction proof for environment rows. set_podman_prepared_create at store/podman.rs 256–278 atomically writes login/home/uid, selected installation facts and pending marker under the exact expected environment entry/binding. Suggested bucket if the suspected write/refusal gap existed: other for unconfirmed cleanup-route loss; no actual loss consequence established. Could-be-highest: potential access to existing user processes/work could matter if a mutation really discarded its sole route, but the inspected concrete writer/mutation routes are source-refuted; no established security or loss-of-work route. Confidence: confirmed narrow source refutation, not runtime observed. proposed_drop: exact source guards and separate-column writes above; no blanket acceptance, no parent drop/lowering accepted. possible_cover: supplied g064/c3 and g065/l3 concern power-loss rollback, a distinct accepted durability boundary not refuted by transactional ordering; g020 approval-time place retarget is likewise a distinct earlier phase, as supplied in g065/l3. This candidate addresses only already-recorded resource references and concurrent catalog writers, not those known issues. No forbidden coverage search, tests, builds or reproductions.
